review.reason:
The artwork maps confidently left-to-right to numbered Holes 1, 2 and 3. The current geometry passes without edits.

Hole 1: The 481-yard dogleg-right par 5 has one substantial lake along the left of the lower fairway and two right-side greenside bunkers. The illustration preserves the shoreline's general extent and the greenside bunker side, although it exaggerates the sand and elongates the approach. The playable corridor remains credible: favoring the right avoids water but brings trees and fairway sand into consideration, while attacking the bend offers a shorter route toward the green.

Hole 2: The dry 413-yard split-fairway par 4 is identifiable by its central tree divider, generous alternative lanes and back-left greenside sand. These defining relationships survive in the artwork. The illustration relocates the fairway bunker toward the left approach, but the available bunker-side control is not a reliable correction for that isolated discrepancy. The broad landing space makes this the forgiving hole, while the tree island still demands a deliberate route and approach position rather than indiscriminate straight-line distance.

Hole 3: The 174-yard par 3 matches the surrounding lake, isolated green and separate foreground landing area with left-side sand. Lake extent and target-to-water proportions are sufficiently consistent. Center-green play provides a sensible conservative target; attacking the left-positioned pin accepts greater water risk. The foreground patch offers staging or recovery space, not a dry route onto the island.

The par-5/4/3 sequence, bending shoreline corridor, dry split route and island carry provide excellent within-round variety. The island repeats course 93, limiting across-days novelty, but its shorter distance and the other two contrasting hole types keep the round sufficiently fresh. Simulated 2/2/1 shots to green and 55/148/26 safe tee options support fair difficulty without proving it; the numbered previews also show usable landing lanes and reasonable targets. No clear greenside bunker reversal or safely correctable lake/proportion mismatch warrants a geometry edit.
